predecessors.name: Gojoseon (Old Joseon)
predecessors.text: Old Chosŏn's heartland around Pyongyang, the seat of the Wiman dynasty's Wanggeom

successors.name: Goguryeo
successors.text: Lelang, 'annexed by Goguryeo under King Micheon' in 313

ledger.x: 108 BCE: Han forces found Lelang Commandery on the ruins of Wiman Joseon at Pyongyang.
82 BCE: Zhenfan is folded into Lelang.
75 BCE: what is left of Lintun passes to Lelang.
32: Daemusin's war for Nangnang reaches the commandery.
37: the fighting over Nangnang ends in Goguryeo's favour until 44.
44: the Eastern Han take Nangnang back from Goguryeo.
204: Gongsun Kang cuts Daifang from Lelang's southern half.
204: Lelang is held by the Gongsun of Liaodong.
245: after the Wei war the Ye come under Lelang and Daifang.
245: the (South) Okjeo tributaries pass under the commanderies.
313: the commandery's tributaries are released with its fall.
313: as for the Ye, the tint ends with the commandery (bridging judgment).
313: the last Chinese commandery on the peninsula ends.

wars.name: Han conquest of Wiman Joseon
wars.outcome: Han victory: 'Han dynasty destroys Wiman Chosŏn in 108 BCE and establishes the Four Commanderies'.

wars.name: Wang Tiao's rebellion in Lelang
wars.outcome: Rebel hold of Lelang from 25 to 30; ended by the governor Wang Zun appointed by Guangwu.

wars.name: Goguryeo-Han war over Nangnang
wars.outcome: Korean chronicle account: Goguryeo defeats Nangnang in 32, destroys it in 37; an Eastern Han army retakes it in 44.

wars.name: Goguryeo-Wei War
wars.outcome: Cao Wei victory: Hwando destroyed; after 245 the Ye and Okjeo tributaries return to the influence of Lelang and Daifang.

wars.name: Goguryeo annexation of Lelang
wars.outcome: Goguryeo annexes the commandery under King Micheon.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary: the commandery is a list of prefectures with a Pyongyang seat, and its southern edge (Pyongyang, Hwanghae or the Han River) is disputed between western and South Korean scholars.
